steps.name: doer
steps.claim: ctx.Doer is the principal recorded as the issue poster.

steps.name: repository
steps.claim: ctx.Repo.Repository is the repository in which the issue is requested.

steps.name: repositoryPermission
steps.claim: ctx.Repo.Permission is the request's repository permission object.

steps.name: issueUnit
steps.claim: unit.TypeIssues identifies the repository issues unit.

steps.name: form
steps.claim: The parsed CreateIssueOption supplies the requested issue fields.

steps.name: issue
steps.claim: A new in-memory issue is initialized for repository with doer as poster and with title, body, ref, and an initially zero deadline.

steps.name: deadline_requested
steps.claim: Deadline handling is conditional on whether the request supplied a deadline.

steps.name: can_write_deadline
steps.claim: The supplied deadline is accepted only when repositoryPermission has write access to the issues unit.

steps.name: deadline_write_result
steps.claim: Only a true write check copies the requested deadline into the issue.

steps.name: copy_deadline
steps.claim: The issue deadline is set from form.Deadline as a timestamp.

steps.name: continue_after_deadline
steps.claim: Processing continues to the separate metadata write check.

steps.name: can_write_metadata
steps.claim: The endpoint separately checks write access to the issues unit before accepting milestone and assignee metadata.

steps.name: metadata_write_result
steps.claim: Writers enter metadata processing; non-writers skip it and have labels cleared.

steps.name: copy_milestone
steps.claim: For an issues-unit writer, the requested milestone is copied to the issue.

steps.name: oneAssignee
steps.claim: form.Assignee is the legacy single-assignee request value.

steps.name: multipleAssignees
steps.claim: form.Assignees is the multiple-assignee request value.

steps.name: resolve_assignee_ids
steps.claim: Requested assignee names are converted to user IDs.

steps.name: assignee_resolution_result
steps.claim: An assignee resolution error terminates the request before issue creation.

steps.name: reject_bad_assignee_names
steps.claim: A missing assignee produces an unprocessable-entity response; other lookup failures produce an internal error, and both return before creation.

steps.name: assigneeID
steps.claim: Each resolved assignee ID is considered in turn.

steps.name: load_assignee
steps.claim: For each resolved ID, the endpoint loads the corresponding user before assignment validation.

steps.name: assignee_lookup_result
steps.claim: A user lookup error terminates before creation.

steps.name: reject_assignee_lookup_failure
steps.claim: Failure to load a resolved assignee returns an internal error before issue creation.

steps.name: assignee
steps.claim: assigneeLookup.user is the loaded candidate assignee.

steps.name: can_be_assigned
steps.claim: Each loaded assignee must be assignable to repository.

steps.name: assignability_result
steps.claim: Lookup failures and non-assignable users terminate before issue creation; successful validations proceed.

steps.name: reject_assignability_failure
steps.claim: An error while checking assignability returns an internal error before issue creation.

steps.name: reject_unassignable_user
steps.claim: A user without access sufficient for assignment produces an unprocessable-entity response before issue creation.

steps.name: clear_labels
steps.claim: When the issues-unit write check is false, the endpoint replaces requested labels with an empty list; it also leaves milestone, deadline, and assignee IDs unset unless set by their separately guarded paths.

steps.name: continue_nonwriter
steps.claim: The non-writer path still proceeds to NewIssue rather than rejecting issue creation locally.

steps.name: new_issue
steps.claim: The endpoint delegates issue creation to issue_service.NewIssue, passing repository, the prepared issue, labels, no attachments, assignee IDs, and requested projects.

steps.name: new_issue_result
steps.claim: A NewIssue error terminates; success may be followed by an optional close operation.

steps.name: reject_new_issue_failure
steps.claim: Blocked-user errors are returned as forbidden, permission-denied or not-exist errors as bad request, and other errors as internal errors; the endpoint returns without its success response.

steps.name: should_close
steps.claim: The newly created issue is closed only when form.Closed is true.

steps.name: close_new_issue
steps.claim: The endpoint delegates closing the newly created issue to issue_service.CloseIssue.

steps.name: close_result
steps.claim: A close failure terminates after creation; otherwise processing continues.

steps.name: reject_close_failure
steps.claim: Open dependencies produce a precondition-failed response and other close failures produce an internal error; the issue may already have been created.

steps.name: refetch_created_issue
steps.claim: After successful creation and any requested close, the endpoint reloads the issue by its assigned ID.

steps.name: refetch_result
steps.claim: A refetch error prevents the success response; a successful refetch returns HTTP 201.

steps.name: reject_refetch_failure
steps.claim: A database error while refetching returns an internal error even though issue creation may already have occurred.

steps.name: created_response
steps.claim: The endpoint returns the converted created issue with HTTP 201 after delegated creation succeeds.

steps.name: writeMode
steps.claim: perm_model.AccessModeWrite is the requested access mode.

steps.name: can_access_write
steps.claim: CanWrite delegates to Permission.CanAccess with write mode and the supplied unit type.

steps.name: return_write_access
steps.claim: CanWrite returns the boolean result of CanAccess for write mode on the supplied unit.

steps.name: requestAssignees
steps.claim: The helper starts with an empty list of requested assignee names.

steps.name: legacy_assignee_branch
steps.claim: The legacy single assignee is appended only when nonempty and not already present in the multiple-assignee list.

steps.name: append_legacy_name
steps.claim: The legacy assignee name is appended to requestAssignees.

steps.name: continue_to_multiple
steps.claim: Processing continues to the multiple-assignee compatibility check.

steps.name: hasNonemptyMultipleAssignees
steps.claim: This source condition is true when the multiple-assignee list has at least one element and its first element is nonempty.

steps.name: append_multiple_branch
steps.claim: The multiple-assignee list is appended only when it is nonempty and its first element is nonempty.

steps.name: append_multiple_names
steps.claim: All supplied multiple-assignee names are appended to requestAssignees.

steps.name: continue_to_resolution
steps.claim: Processing continues to name resolution.

steps.name: doNotIgnoreMissing
steps.claim: The helper passes false for ignoreNonExistent, so a missing named user is not silently skipped.

steps.name: get_user_ids
steps.claim: The helper returns GetUserIDsByNames for the assembled names with ignoreNonExistent false.

steps.name: return_resolved_assignees
steps.claim: The resolved ID list and any lookup error are returned unchanged.

steps.name: query_user_by_id
steps.claim: The helper queries the user table for the supplied ID.

steps.name: query_result
steps.claim: Database errors are returned; no row becomes ErrUserNotExist; a found row returns the loaded user.

steps.name: return_database_error
steps.claim: The database error is returned with no user.

steps.name: return_missing_user
steps.claim: ErrUserNotExist for the supplied ID is returned with no user.

steps.name: user
steps.claim: The queried row is the loaded user.

steps.name: return_user
steps.claim: The loaded user is returned with a nil error.

steps.name: route
steps.claim: The shown API handler is CreateIssue for POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues.

steps.name: parse-form
steps.claim: The handler obtains the API CreateIssue form from the request context.

steps.name: deadline-write-check
steps.claim: When a deadline is supplied, the handler checks whether the repository permission can write the issues unit before retaining the deadline.

steps.name: deadline-branch
steps.claim: Deadline retention is conditional on both a supplied deadline and the issues-unit write check; otherwise the deadline remains unset.

steps.name: issue
steps.claim: The handler constructs a repository issue resource from the repository, authenticated doer, and form fields; its deadline field is the conditionally retained deadline.

steps.name: issue-write-check
steps.claim: Before applying milestone and assignee processing, the handler checks whether the repository permission can write the issues unit.

steps.name: writer-branch
steps.claim: The handler has a writer branch and a non-writer branch; the latter clears labels but does not itself reject issue creation.

steps.name: create-issue
steps.claim: The handler invokes the issue service to create the issue, passing the repository, issue object, labels, no assignee object, resolved assignee IDs, and projects.

steps.name: create-result
steps.claim: A creation error causes an API error response and return; successful creation continues to optional closure and response construction.

steps.name: closed-branch
steps.claim: After successful creation, the handler optionally closes the issue when the request asks for a closed issue.

steps.name: set-deadline
steps.claim: The supplied deadline is converted to a timestamp and retained because the issues-unit write check succeeded.

steps.name: clear-deadline
steps.claim: No deadline timestamp is retained when the deadline is absent or the issues-unit write check is false.

steps.name: set-milestone
steps.claim: The writer branch copies the requested milestone identifier to the issue.

steps.name: resolve-assignees
steps.claim: The writer branch resolves the legacy and plural assignee names into assignee IDs.

steps.name: assignee-resolution
steps.claim: An assignee-resolution error returns from the handler; otherwise each resolved assignee is checked for repository assignability.

steps.name: clear-labels
steps.claim: The non-writer branch clears labels rather than denying the create request.

steps.name: post-create-close
steps.claim: Successful creation proceeds to the close branch or directly to refetch and the created response.

steps.name: creation-failure
steps.claim: A non-nil NewIssue error causes an API error response and prevents the success response.

steps.name: close-issue
steps.claim: If the request marks the issue closed, the handler invokes CloseIssue after creation.

steps.name: close-result
steps.claim: A close error returns from the handler; a successful close continues to refetch and serialize the issue.

steps.name: refetch-issue
steps.claim: When no close is requested, the handler refetches the created issue before responding.

steps.name: serialize-response
steps.claim: The handler converts the refetched issue into the API response.

steps.name: created-response
steps.claim: The shown handler returns HTTP 201 after successful creation, optional closure, refetch, and serialization.

steps.name: load-assignee
steps.claim: For each resolved assignee ID, the handler loads the user record.

steps.name: check-assignability
steps.claim: For each loaded assignee, the handler checks whether that user can be assigned in the repository.

steps.name: assignability-result
steps.claim: A non-assignable assignee returns an API validation error; an assignable assignee permits continuation to issue creation.

steps.name: assignee-resolution-failure
steps.claim: An assignee resolution error returns from the handler before issue creation; the shown branch maps a missing user to a validation response and other errors to an internal response.

steps.name: assignee-check-complete
steps.claim: The current assignee passed the repository assignability check; iteration over any remaining assignees continues in the same manner.

steps.name: assignee-validation-failure
steps.claim: A user who cannot be assigned to the repository causes an API validation error and prevents issue creation.

steps.name: close-failure
steps.claim: A CloseIssue error causes an API error response and prevents the created success response.

steps.name: refetch-after-close
steps.claim: After successful closure, the handler refetches the issue before responding.

steps.name: serialize-after-close
steps.claim: The handler converts the refetched issue into the API response.

steps.name: created-response-after-close
steps.claim: The shown handler returns HTTP 201 after successful creation and closure, refetch, and serialization.

arguments.reason: Repair the accepted CanWrite invocations with the caller's permission configuration and the source objects used as unit-type arguments.
Reread the retained CreateIssue body to correct the unbound deadline permission argument before linking.

The retained CreateIssue caller maps form.Deadline, a request field, to the CanWrite helper's unitType parameter, but the source call passes the literal issues unit (unit.TypeIssues). No existing caller object of the required value type represents that literal, so this link cannot be repaired without revising the retained caller interpretation to bind the source-supported unit constant and then relinking all three question copies.

The retained caller maps form.Deadline to the helper's unitType parameter, but form.Deadline is not the source's unit.TypeIssues value. I will revise the caller to bind/use the issues unit type before linking; no valid current caller object supports this link as written.
Repair the retained CreateIssue entry interpretation by binding the issues unit type explicitly and preserving the route, write checks, creation effect, close exception, and response path.
